_comment: The always-on context budget (FR-073). Read by pack/scripts/context-budget.py.
WHY A RATCHET AND NOT A CEILING. The defect this gates (PACK-R) is silent
ACCUMULATION -- each doc looks free at the moment it is written, so the total grows
unnoticed. An absolute ceiling is a poor fit for that shape: it stays quiet through
the entire accumulation and then red-lights an ordinary paragraph, which teaches
people to raise the ceiling reflexively -- the exact habit the gate exists to break.
The ratchet fails on unacknowledged GROWTH instead. Exceeding the baseline is not an
error; leaving the baseline unchanged while exceeding it is. The fix is one line in a
diff (`context-budget.py gate --update-baseline`), so growth stays cheap but never
stays invisible: a reviewer sees `always_on_tokens: 43708 -> 46200` and can ask why.
The ratchet also works DOWNWARD. A baseline that only rises is a ceiling wearing a
different hat, so the gate reports when the set has shrunk enough that the baseline
THE BACKSTOP IS DERIVED, NOT CHOSEN. ceiling_tokens is the point past which the
always-on set stops fitting the smallest model tier the roster delegates to:
Rounded to 60000. Change the derivation inputs, not the answer.
